model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Takano: a D+7 seat, incumbency, and a clear money advantage, with markets pricing his re-election at roughly 94%. With no polls or ratings to contradict that picture, the race stays in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Takano or unexpectedly strong Republican fundraising could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark Takano, the Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a Riverside-area district that leans Democratic by about seven points. He has raised roughly $894,000 and holds a cash advantage, while Republican Steve Manos reports little visible fundraising and no outside groups are spending against the incumbent. Prediction markets give the Democrat about a 94% chance of winning.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the forecast rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and the money gap. Those fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic win, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
